description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT=30), found while quantifying temperature-grid thinning. Regression-locked by
tests/thermal_temperature_thinning.rs::production_interpolation_leaves_the_bracket_above_half_an_ev. NOT FIXED --
it needs its own change and its own V&V.

THE DEFECT. sigma_inel(E,T) is monotone in T across the tabulated grid, so an interpolated value at a temperature
between two tabulated ones MUST lie between their two cross sections. The production interpolation does not:

  at 393.15 K, E = 3.9 eV:  interpolated 4.4175 b   against the bracket [4.6097, 4.6367]
                            -- roughly 4-5% BELOW the lower bracketing value, i.e. outside it entirely

Same behaviour at 523.15 K, 900 K and 1400 K. About 1% low at 0.5 eV. CORRECT at and below 0.1 eV.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN CAUGHT. The existing coverage (tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs) checks 0.0253 eV only,
which is inside the region where the interpolation behaves. The defect lives above ~0.5 eV.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERY non-tabulated temperature request today. The graphite evaluation tabulates 296, 400, 500, 600,
700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000 K; the IAEA HTR-10 B1-B4 benchmarks are at 293.15 / 393.15 / 523.15 K, all of which
are interpolated. So this is on the HTR-10 critical path, not a corner case.

SEVERITY IN CONTEXT: at 0.0253 eV, where the thermal spectrum lives, the interpolation is fine, and coherent elastic
(~90% of the thermal cross section) is unaffected. The error is in the epithermal tail of the inelastic channel. It
is a real defect and a bounded one -- do not report it as breaking the thermal spectrum without measuring that.

NOT THE CAUSE, already ruled out by the reporting agent: zero-endpoint handling. A PreserveZeros variant gave
bit-identical statistics, and the reconstruction was verified monotone. What was NOT established is why ln S is so
non-linear in T in the far tail -- only that it is. Start there.

RELATED: op-cjw.22 (inelastic temperature interpolation) is filed P4 on the stated assumption that target temps are
tabulated exactly. That assumption fails for HTR-10, and this bead is direct evidence the interpolation it defers is
actually wrong rather than merely absent. Consider re-prioritising or merging.

Also fixed in passing while measuring this, and worth knowing: IncoherentInelastic was DISCARDING the inelastic LI
temperature-interpolation codes -- the same class of defect as op-1y4y on the elastic side. mf7.rs now retains them
(IncoherentInelastic::temp_interp), so the tape's own LI=4 is read rather than assumed.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: READ UPSTREAM FIRST (2026-09-10), result: NJOY2016 THERMR has NO temperature interpolation of S(alpha,beta) at all. thermr.f90 main loop (l.347-350) requires the PENDF to carry a block at the desired temperature ('desired temperature not on tape'), and calcem (l.1720-1741) walks the MF7 temperature blocks with 'do while (abs(t-temp).gt.temp/500)' and errors 'desired temperature not found' unless a tabulated temperature lies within 0.2% of the request (it then uses that block and prints 'difference between temperatures desired and found is ...'). So the LI=4 'ln S linear in T' interpolation whose output leaves the bracket above 0.5 eV is a PORT-ONLY extension with no upstream behaviour to reproduce; NJOY users get HTR-10's 393.15 K by running LEAPR at that temperature (this crate has a LEAPR port) or by accepting the nearest tabulated block. Implication for the fix: the upstream-faithful options are (a) refuse/snap to the nearest tabulated T with a message (exactly what NJOY does), or (b) generate S(a,b) at the exact T with LEAPR; if interpolation is kept, note that interpolating ln S at FIXED (alpha,beta) and then integrating with T-dependent kinematics (alpha,beta scale with 1/kT) is not guaranteed to stay inside the bracket of sigma(E,T1)/sigma(E,T2) - interpolating the integrated sigma_inel(E,T) (or the whole integrated kernel) in T between the two tabulated temperatures is bracketed by construction. Not fixed in this session; the regression test stays as the lock.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
FIXED 2026-09-10. Decision: keep the maintainer's 2026-08-11 interpolate-inside-the-grid policy (HTR-10 needs 393.15/523.15 K and NJOY has no interpolation to match - see the previous comment: calcem refuses beyond temp/500), but move the interpolation from S(alpha,beta) at fixed table coordinates to the EVALUATED quantities. Root cause confirmed by the fix: with LAT=1 the table's (alpha,beta) are in units of kT0, so a fixed table point is a different physical transfer at each T; interpolating ln S there and integrating with the target temperature's kinematics is not bracketed. Now parse_mf7_at_temperature keeps BOTH bracketing tabulated tables (IncoherentInelastic::temperature_bracket {t_lo_k, t_hi_k, li, s_lo, s_hi}, alongside the fixed-grid s_tables for table-level consumers), and inelastic.rs evaluates double_differential and cross_section at each tabulated temperature with that temperature's own S, kinematics and T_eff, then interpolates the two RESULTS in T with the evaluation's LI law (log-lin for MAT 30). sigma_inel is therefore a scalar interpolation of the two endpoint integrals - bracketed by construction; the kernel (and hence the ACE emission bins) is the same interpolation pointwise. Tabulated requests are unchanged (no bracket, single-temperature worker).

MEASURED (graphite MAT 30, 393.15 K, natom=1; bracket = [sigma(296 K), sigma(400 K)]): 0.001 eV 0.5230 in [0.3017, 0.5437]; 0.005 eV 0.3567 in [0.2204, 0.3690]; 0.0253 eV 0.6797 in [0.4864, 0.6960]; 0.1 eV 1.9537 in [1.5936, 1.9819]; 0.5 eV 3.9838 in [3.7915, 3.9978]; 1 eV 4.3601 in [4.2625, 4.3670]; 3.9 eV 4.6349 in [4.6097, 4.6367] (was 4.4175, 4.2% below). Each value equals the LI=4 combination lo^(1-w) hi^w with w=(393.15-296)/104 to 1e-9. The regression test was renamed production_interpolation_stays_inside_its_bracket and now asserts bracketing at all seven energies, the closed-form LI combination, kernel bracketing pointwise at (0.5->0.45 eV, mu=-0.9/0/0.9), and that a tabulated 400 K request carries no bracket and is bit-identical to before. Docs: src/thermr/mf7.rs module policy step 2, src/thermr/README.md caveat, verification_and_validation/thermal_temperature_grid_thinning.md addendum (the study's own SabTemperatureStack numbers are unaffected - it interpolates S at fixed (alpha,beta) by design to measure that table-level error).

NOT CHANGED, noted: the snap tolerance stays rdelas's T/1000+5 K (293.15 K -> 296 K block), looser than calcem's T/500 which alone would refuse 293.15 K for graphite. No NJOY oracle exists for an interpolated temperature; the evaluation's own tabulated brackets are the only check, and that is what the test uses. Cost: kernel evaluation doubles at interpolated temperatures only.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Landed in 65ac7065 on develop. Root cause was WHERE the interpolation happened, not the law: it interpolated S(alpha,beta) at fixed table coordinates and then integrated with the target temperature's kinematics. Under LAT=1 the table's (alpha,beta) are in units of kT0, so a fixed table point is a different physical transfer at each T and the integral is not bracketed. Now parse_mf7_at_temperature keeps both bracketing tabulated tables and inelastic.rs evaluates at each with its own S, kinematics and T_eff, then interpolates the two results with the evaluation's LI law - bracketed by construction. Re-measured at 393.15 K: 3.9 eV 4.6349 in [4.6097, 4.6367]; 1 eV 4.3601 in [4.2625, 4.3670]; 0.5 eV 3.9838 in [3.7915, 3.9978]; 0.0253 eV 0.6797 in [0.4864, 0.6960]. Verified independently by the coordinator: GRAPHITE_TSL_DIR set, all 8 thermal_temperature_thinning tests ran and passed (they SKIP silently without that variable). Upstream note: thermr.f90 never interpolates in temperature at all - calcem refuses any MF=7 block farther than T/500 - so this remains a port extension, now at least bracketed by its own evaluation.

description:
Nothing hands a particle from one tracking method to another.

delta_flight (keff_delta.rs:468-495) samples, advances the FULL distance, then looks up - no boundary test at all. track_to_collision (delta_tracking.rs:305-316) reports escaped=true when the lookup returns None (:327-335) but returns a position PAST the boundary, not on it, so it cannot serve as-is.

Needs: advance, test against the CSG region boundary, TRUNCATE at the intersection, hand off. Geometry::distance_to_boundary (geometry.rs:255) is the right tool and has zero callers from any delta code.

description:
Prophylactic, from the op-hc2o post-mortem (2026-08-14).

Two defects in that bead's step 5 were the SAME class of failure: physics that is implemented, tested at unit level, and then never actually invoked by the path that matters.

- Nuclide::sample_thermal was implemented, had 7 green V&V tests at nuclide level, and had exactly ONE caller in the crate (physics::transport_csg). Both k-eigenvalue paths -- physics::keff and pebble_beds::keff_delta -- silently fell through to free-gas kinematics for 3.5 months.
- The one test that would have caught it was #[ignore]d for a reason that was itself wrong (a nuclide NAMING error, "C12" vs the real "C0", misdiagnosed as a missing-data gap and attributed to a bead that was never even filed).

Neither showed up as a failure. Everything was green the whole time.

WHAT TO ADD:
1. A test that asserts every collision path routes thermal scattering. Concretely: for each of the transport entry points (run_keff, run_keff_delta, transport_csg), run a short fixed case with a moderator nuclide carrying an S(alpha,beta) table and assert the result DIFFERS from the same case without it. A bit-identical result is the exact signature of a dead branch and is trivially detectable -- that is what caught this one.
2. A guard against silently-ignored tests. #[ignore] on a V&V test hid a defect for months. Options: a periodic '--ignored' sweep in the suite runner, or a rule that an #[ignore] reason naming a bead must reference a bead that EXISTS (op-wqk.21 did not).
3. Consider a general audit for other implemented-but-uncalled physics. grep for pub fns in src/physics/ and src/material/ whose only callers are tests. sample_thermal would have shown up.

Not urgent, but this class of bug is invisible to the existing gates by construction, and the workspace has now been bitten by it once at P1 severity on the HTR-10 critical path.
title: outram-mc: no regression gate stops a thermal-scattering law from being wired with no caller

description:
gh:#194 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/194 — likely ROOT CAUSE of op-77pu / gh:#188, and of the same one-signed narrowness measured on graphite (op-x77y).

FOUND BY building NJOY2016 from source and reading it (2016.79 18Mar25, gfortran 16.2.1, cmake 4.4.3, Release, clean build at ~/Documents/research/NJOY2016/build/njoy).

WHAT NJOY DOES (src/thermr.f90):
  module header: 'generate an energy grid for the secondary energy distribution
    integrated over angle ADAPTIVELY. The angular distribution for each secondary
    energy is given using a set of EQUALLY PROBABLE EMISSION COSINES.'
  calcem (:1541): incident grid FIXED at 118 points (ngrid=118, the egrid array);
    secondary-energy grid built by ADAPTIVE BISECTION at label 330, halving a
    panel until linear interpolation agrees to tol, nemax=5000, imax=20 levels;
    tol read from the input card (reference-data decks use 0.001).
  sigl (:2660): 'Compute the cross section and legendre components or
    equally-probable ANGLES for the scattering from e to ep.' s(1)=sum is the
    kernel value at that (E,E'); the equiprobable construction (nbin=nl-1,
    fract=sum/nbin) partitions the ANGULAR distribution at fixed (E,E').

WHAT WE DO (src/material/thermal.rs):
  N_EMIT_GRID = 384 incident energies (3.3x finer than NJOY's 118)
  N_OUTGOING  = 64 EQUIPROBABLE DISCRETE outgoing energies; line ~433 'A scatter
    is sampled by choosing one of the n_out outgoing energies uniformly'
  N_COSINES   = equiprobable cosines (this axis matches NJOY)

So we applied NJOY's ANGULAR representation to the ENERGY axis.

WHY IT EXPLAINS EVERY RECORDED SYMPTOM: representative points lie INSIDE the
distribution so both tails truncate by construction -> one-signed narrow; the
error falls as ~1/n_out with NO plateau (a discretisation error, not convergence);
it does not respond to N_EMIT_GRID at all (-11.6 % at 16 bins whether the incident
grid held 48 or 1536); and a discrete outgoing-energy set cannot satisfy detailed
balance against a continuum, which is the wrong equilibrium temperature in
tests/thermal_kernel_stationary_distribution.rs. Effort is also in the wrong
dimension: 384->1536 incident moves rms width 0.07 points, 16->128 outgoing moves
worst case ~10 points.

DOC-COMMENT ERROR TO FIX IN THE SAME CHANGE. thermal.rs:187 says 'The proper fix
is a continuous outgoing-energy law (NJOY iform = 1)'. Direction right,
attribution WRONG: iform=1 is E-mu-E' / MF6 Law7 (fixed mu grid, adaptive E' per
mu, added in NJOY2010). What is wanted is what the STANDARD iform=0 already does
on the energy axis. Implementing that comment literally builds Law7 ordering and
does not fix the narrowness.

FIX: replace the equiprobable outgoing-energy table with a tabulated cumulative
distribution in E' sampled by interpolation, grid built by calcem's
bisection-to-tolerance criterion. KEEP the equiprobable cosines. Then consider
reducing N_EMIT_GRID toward 118, since the incident axis is over-resolved
relative to where the error lives.

DO NOT DECLARE IT FIXED FROM THE MECHANISM. Per the method that closed gh:#193,
PRICE it: implement behind a flag and measure the width against the same THERMR
oracle. Twenty-one correct accuracy statements missed #193.

NOT CHECKED: the tol=0.001 above is from the WIMSR deck in reference-data/; I did
not confirm which tol generated the graphite/water golden tables. If it differs,
the adaptive grid density differs with it.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED 81c6a14c / 2dd912fb, and the attribution in this bead was REFUTED by measurement. Both halves matter.

RIGHT: the representation was lossy and it mattered. ThermalScattering::sample read back one of N discrete outgoing energies, losing all intra-bin variance. Interpolating the quantile function between those nodes moved the FHR pebble from -469 pcm to +37 pcm (0.2 sigma) against OpenMC. Trajectory +4004 -> -469 -> +37.

WRONG: this bead and gh:#194 said it looked like the root cause of op-77pu / gh:#188. It is not. Kernel width vs NJOY2016 MF=6: graphite -2.33% -> -1.96%, H2O -4.91% -> -4.02%. Roughly 80% of the width deficit SURVIVES the change, so it is in the THERMR kernel underneath, not in how this crate samples the table. op-77pu stays open and is not explained by this.

FACTUAL CORRECTION to this bead's description: I described NJOY as using an adaptive interpolated E' grid with equiprobable reserved for cosines, and ours as having applied the angular representation to the energy axis. Sharper statement from 81c6a14c: equiprobable_emission inverts the cumulative at bin MIDPOINTS, e_out[k] = Q((k+1/2)/N) - the quantile function sampled at N points, not a histogram of edges. The defect was narrower than framed: not the wrong representation, but failing to INTERPOLATE the quantile function that representation tabulates.

ALSO REFUTED in the same work, recorded so the resolution is not spent again: subdividing every E' interval 4x (graphite -2.01%, H2O -3.85%) and raising the mu quadrature NMU 200->800 (graphite -1.96%, H2O -3.87%). Neither is the cause.

The hard condition written into this bead - PRICE it, do not argue from mechanism - is what caught the wrong attribution. Keeping that condition on op-rpb6-adjacent work.

title: outram-mc: outgoing-energy law uses NJOY's ANGULAR representation — replace equiprobable bins with an adaptive interpolated CDF

description:
IAPWS-IF97 Region 5 requires explicit backward equations to compute temperature from pressure and enthalpy, and from pressure and entropy. These equations are currently missing from tampines-steam-tables. This issue also covers a related explicit near-critical Region 4 (h,s) flash, to replace the iterative pressure fallback near the critical point.

Scope:
1. Region 5 backward equations - T(p,h) and T(p,s) for high-temperature water/steam.
2. Region 4 near-critical (h,s) flash - explicit p(h,s), Tsat(p), and vapor-quality x(h,s) for 623.15 <= Tsat <= 647.04 K, replacing the iterative pressure-fallback path in that near-critical band.

Three prototypes (ChatGPT/NUS ChatGPT Edu-assisted) posted as comments on GitHub issue #34:
- Python prototype: Region 5 forward equations + T_ph_5/T_ps_5 Chebyshev fit + validate() routine
- region5_backward_explicit.rs: direct Rust transcription of the Region 5 backward fit
- region4_hs_nearcritical_explicit.rs: p_hs_4_nearcritical, tsat_p_4, x_hs_4_nearcritical

Fit domains:
- Region 5: 1e-4 <= p <= 50 MPa, 1073.15 <= T <= 2273.15 K
- Region 4 near-critical: 623.15 <= Tsat <= 647.04 K

Not an official IAPWS supplementary release - needs review, integration into the Rust crate, and independent validation against IAPWS-IF97 reference data before it can be trusted.

Follow-up work:
- Port the fitted Chebyshev coefficients / evaluation logic into crates/tampines-steam-tables as Rust
- Add unit tests validating against forward equations and published IAPWS-IF97 reference data where available
- Document methodology + results per the workspace V&V documentation rule

GitHub issue: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/34
title: Tampines steam tables: explicit backward equations — Region 5 T(p,h)/T(p,s) and Region 4 near-critical (h,s) flash
